translationRepairs: When war broke out on the coast, he accompanied Governor Yuxie to Zhejiang.
When war broke out on the coast, he accompanied Governor Yuqian to Zhejiang.
s0092 names 總督裕謙; 謙 is qian, so Yuxie misromanizes the personal name, and Yuqian restores the standard reading without changing the rest of the sentence.
When coastal military affairs arose, he followed Governor Yuxie to Zhejiang.
When coastal military affairs arose, he followed Governor Yuqian to Zhejiang.
The same 裕謙 appears in the literal English as Yuxie; correcting to Yuqian matches the Chinese name while leaving the surrounding calque intact.

After Yuxie died in battle, Huang was implicated and exiled to Yili; when Lin Zexu was sent to the same frontier and colonization was proposed, Huang helped manage the irrigation works with distinction and was eventually pardoned and allowed to return.

After Yuqian died in battle, Huang was implicated and exiled to Yili; when Lin Zexu was sent to the same frontier and colonization was proposed, Huang helped manage the irrigation works with distinction and was eventually pardoned and allowed to return.
s0093 opens with 裕謙死難; replacing the repeated Yuxie with Yuqian corrects the same misreading of 謙 without altering the rest of the idiomatic sentence.

Yuxie died in the line of duty; Mian was implicated and sent in exile to Yili; soon Lin Zexu also arrived in exile; when colonization farming was proposed, Mian assisted in managing waterworks with merit and was pardoned and returned.

Yuqian died in the line of duty; Mian was implicated and sent in exile to Yili; soon Lin Zexu also arrived in exile; when colonization farming was proposed, Mian assisted in managing waterworks with merit and was pardoned and returned.
The literal likewise begins from 裕謙; Yuqian is the accurate romanization, and the remainder already tracks 死難…遣戍伊犁…林則徐…屯田…水利…赦還.
Yao studied under his kinsman Yao Nai, cared little for pedantic textual scholarship, sought the larger meaning, and put it into practice.
Yao studied under his collateral ancestor Yao Nai, cared little for pedantic textual scholarship, sought the larger meaning, and put it into practice.
瑩師事從祖鼐 uses 從祖, a specific collateral paternal-ancestor kinship term, not a vague kinsman; collateral ancestor Yao Nai restores that sense and matches the unit’s literal.
